1r1tc1i: Ser, estar, tener, and hay: four verbs, four jobs
ymd3fu: To describe people and places you need four verbs, and each has its own job. **Ser** says what or how someone or something is: identity, origin, profession, personality, appearance (**Mi hermana es alta y muy simpática**).
9rn6h4: **Estar** says where someone or something is (**Mi casa está cerca del lago**). **Tener** says what a person has: family, age, things, features (**Tengo dos hermanos**, **Mi abuelo tiene ochenta años**, **Tiene el pelo corto**). **Hay** says what exists in a place, with new information (**En mi barrio hay un mercado**).
13rc77o: The question that helps you choose: **cómo es**? → ser; **dónde está**? → estar; **qué tiene** / **cuántos años tiene**? → tener; **qué hay** there? → hay.
10t5vr3: When you describe someone, use all three: **es** (what they're like), **tiene** (what they have), and **está** (where they are now). It sounds complete and natural.
cjmtpw: _Mi hermano_ is a specific person: **está**. _Hay_ only with new information (_un, una, dos_…).
ptol70: Personality and appearance of a person = **ser**.
1kcch6t: The possessives **mi, tu, su** agree in number with the thing possessed, not with the person: **mi hermano**, **mis hermanos**. **Nuestro** and **vuestro** also agree in gender: **nuestra casa**, **nuestros padres**.
1sq839m: **Su** has many possible owners: his, her, your (usted), their (ellos, ellas), your (ustedes). If it's not clear, clarify with **de** + person: **la casa de él**, **la casa de Ana**.
15saj8j: Adjectives agree in gender and number with the noun: **un tío alto**, **una tía alta**, **unos primos altos**. Those ending in **-e** or a consonant don't change in the feminine: **una hermana inteligente**, **una amiga joven** (but **jóvenes** in the plural). Also remember nationalities: **español → española**.
1wgkuse: The adjective agrees with _abuelas_: feminine plural.
9ulvqb: The present tense of your week: -ar, -er, -ir, and reflexive
crlf87: Your whole day fits in the present tense. **-ar** verbs have **-a-** in the endings (_trabajo, trabajas, trabaja_…); **-er** and **-ir** verbs have **-e-** (_como, comes, come; vivo, vives, vive_), and only separate in nosotros and vosotros: **comemos / vivimos**, **coméis / vivís**.
1g69z3m: Reflexive verbs are the same, but with **me, te, se, nos, os, se** in front: **me levanto**, **nos acostamos**. Remember the blocks with vowel change: **me despierto**, **me acuesto**.
1ex5w75: To talk about habits, add frequency: **siempre**, **casi siempre**, **normalmente**, **a veces**, **casi nunca**, **nunca**. With _nunca_ there are two positions: **Nunca como carne** or **No como carne nunca**. And to place the action in time: **a las ocho**, **los lunes**, **por la mañana**.
1w4e7hb: The time of an action goes with **a**: _a las ocho_; the time right now, with **es / son**: _son las ocho_.
htfari: Three regular verbs and one reflexive
9l3slz: A voice message almost always has the same shape: **greeting** (_¡Hola! Soy Mateo_), **reason** (_te llamo por lo del sábado_), **details** (place, time, who), and **goodbye** (_¡Nos vemos!_, _Un beso_). If you know this shape, you know where the important information is: in the middle.
1x3ydl0: Before listening, prepare three questions: **¿Dónde?**, **¿A qué hora?**, and **¿Qué plan?** While listening, don't try to understand everything: note only numbers, times, place names, and the prepositions that go with them (_enfrente de, detrás de_…).
1pz1j0m: Listen twice. The first time, to know who is speaking and why. The second, to complete your notes. Watch for changes of plan: words like **pero**, **no**, or **mejor** announce that something changes.
1jyjc8o: If the message gives two times, the last one you hear after **pero** or **mejor** is usually the right one.
qha2ey: Translating everything makes you lose the important details. Look only for the answers to your three questions.

1jtqvfv: Review: c/z/s, b/v, r/rr, and the jota
1hayhqg: In these four weeks you have worked on four difficult points. **C, Z, and S**: in almost all of Latin America and in parts of Andalusia and the Canary Islands, _casa_ and _caza_ sound the same (**seseo**); in central and northern Spain, _ce, ci, za, zo, zu_ sound like the _th_ in _think_ (**distinción**). Both are correct.
5gvdk7: **B and V** are the same sound throughout the Spanish-speaking world: _vaca_ and _baca_ are pronounced the same. At the beginning of a sentence or after _m, n_ the lips close (_un vaso_); between vowels they barely touch (_la vaca, el lobo_).
13s3erp: **R and RR**: one tap (_pero, caro_) or several (_perro, carro, Roma, Enrique_). **J and G**: _jueves, gente_ with jota; _gato, guitarra_ with soft g. In Guatemala the jota is soft, almost an aspirated _h_.
qeav6u: This week you put the four sounds together in real sentences about family, places, and routine. Go slowly first and then at normal speed.
1ko7nga: Four writing rules: **z** before a, o, u and **c** before e, i (_zapato, cine_); **b** or **v** are learned with the word (_vivir, beber_); **rr** only between vowels; **j** always with a, o, u (_jamón, joven, jugo_) and **g** or **j** before e, i (_gente, jefe_).
1vlv7hp: No **v** is bitten: _vive, bebe_ sound the same. Between vowels, relaxed lips.
1t5i6qz: Choose seseo (_Ignasio, cosina, plasa, dose_) or distinción with _th_. Be consistent throughout the sentence.
1rz6od5: Strong: _Rodrigo, corre, perro_ and the first r of _alrededor_ (after l). Single: _primo_ and the final r of _alrededor_.
g81gq2: Five jotas: _jueves, hija, juega, gente, jardín_. Soft or strong, but never the English _j_.
135pdhg: All together: soft **v** between vowels in _levanto_; **s** in _seis_; jota in _jugo_ and _naranja_; and a single r in _naranja_.
